summary: The article follows two young borrowers, Nicole Plauché and Marisa Johnson, who are struggling to afford holiday gifts now that the COVID-era student loan payment pause has ended. It relays advice from Credit Karma's Courtney Alev on budgeting, talking openly with family, choosing experiences over gifts, using credit responsibly, and finding cheap or homemade gift options.
one_line: With student loan payments resumed, young borrowers like Marisa Johnson cut holiday spending, and a Credit Karma expert offers budgeting and low-cost gift tips.
key_facts: Marisa Johnson, 26, has approximately $145,000 in student loan debt from her bachelor's and master's degrees.
Johnson has paid $300 a month since the COVID-era payment pause ended in October, while she waits to see if she'll be enrolled in a new income-driven repayment plan.
Johnson is a non-profit worker in Citrus Heights, California, and is combining gifts with her older sister or choosing affordable gifts.
Nicole Plauché is described as a tech sales manager from Dallas, Texas, who is a mom and new grad; her family's love language is gift giving.
The Biden administration ended the three-year student loan payment pause, forcing millions of people to resume payments.
Courtney Alev, consumer financial advocate at Credit Karma, recommends the 50-30-20 budget: 50% necessities, 30% wants, 20% savings and debt repayment.
Alev advises taking holiday gift money only from the 30% portion of the budget and planning ahead; Microsoft Office offers a holiday spending budget template.
Alev warns that resentment can build if people buy gifts while barely making student loan payments, and urges talking openly with loved ones.
Plauché has told her family she won't be able to give gifts this year, and is avoiding her credit card to avoid more debt.
Suggested low-cost experiences include a hike, free city events, a holiday movie marathon, a free museum visit, or a volunteering day.
Alev recommends setting a budget for each credit card, knowing payment due dates, and being intentional with buy now, pay later services.
Johnson is gifting a used book to her dad and painting something for her mom, since she already owns the painting tools.
